plan.ja: 楚の[[p:沈尹戌]]は、自分が呉の舟を焼いて退路を断つ間、[[p:囊瓦]]に川を挟んで守るよう説いた。だが功を独り占めしたい囊瓦は川を渡って攻め、呉は三度戦って三度破った。柏挙では呉王の弟夫概が王の許しを待たず五千で突っ込み、楚軍を崩した。呉軍は五度戦って五度勝ち、郢に入った。
plan.en: [[p:沈尹戌|Shen Yin Xu]] of Chu proposed that [[p:囊瓦|Nang Wa]] hold the river while he burned the Wu boats behind them. Nang Wa, wanting the glory for himself, crossed and attacked; Wu beat him three times. At Boju the king's brother Fugai charged with five thousand without waiting for leave and broke the Chu army. Fighting five battles and winning all five, Wu entered Ying.

tales.ja: [[p:孫武]]は呉王[[p:闔閭]]に兵法を説いたとき、宮中の女官百八十人を二隊に分けて調練し、笑って命に従わない隊長の寵姫二人を王の制止も聞かず斬った。以後、女官たちは一糸乱れず動いたという。
tales.en: When [[p:孫武|Sun Wu]] laid out the art of war for King [[p:闔閭|Helü]], he drilled a hundred and eighty palace women in two companies and, over the king's protests, beheaded the two favourites who led them for laughing at his orders. After that the women moved as one.

tales.ja: 郢に入った[[p:伍子胥]]は、父と兄を殺した平王の墓をあばいて屍に鞭打った。友の[[p:申包胥]]が「天理に背く」と責めると、「日暮れて道遠し、ゆえに倒行逆施す」と答えた。
tales.en: In Ying [[p:伍子胥|Wu Zixu]] dug up the body of King Ping, who had killed his father and brother, and flogged it. When his old friend [[p:申包胥|Shen Baoxu]] called it an outrage against heaven, he answered: "The day is late and the road is long; so I walk backwards and act against the grain."

after.ja: 楚の昭王は逃れ、[[p:申包胥]]の嘆願で秦の援軍が来ると、呉は郢を去った。この勝利で呉は南方の強国となった。
after.en: King Zhao of Chu fled; when [[p:申包胥|Shen Baoxu]] brought a Qin army with his pleading, Wu left Ying. The victory made Wu a great power of the south.

deploy.ja: 斉は[[p:田忌]]を将、[[p:孫臏]]を軍師として韓を救うため魏の都大梁を突いた。魏の[[p:龐涓]]は韓から兵を返し、太子申とともに斉軍を追った。
deploy.en: Qi sent [[p:田忌|Tian Ji]], with [[p:孫臏|Sun Bin]] as his strategist, to strike at the Wei capital Daliang and so relieve Han. [[p:龐涓|Pang Juan]] of Wei pulled back from Han and, with the crown prince Shen, went after the Qi army.

plan.ja: [[p:孫臏]]は「魏の兵は斉を臆病と侮っている」と見て、初日は十万、翌日は五万、三日目は三万と、毎夜かまどの数を減らして見せた。[[p:龐涓]]は「斉兵は三日で半分以上逃げた」と喜び、歩兵を置いて騎兵だけで追った。孫臏は日暮れに着くと読んだ狭い馬陵の道に、一万の弩兵を伏せた。
plan.en: [[p:孫臏|Sun Bin]] saw that Wei thought Qi's soldiers cowards. He had the army light a hundred thousand cooking fires the first night, fifty thousand the second, thirty thousand the third. "Half the men of Qi have deserted in three days!" [[p:龐涓|Pang Juan]] rejoiced, left his foot behind and pursued with the horse alone. Sun Bin hid ten thousand crossbowmen along the narrow road at Maling, where he reckoned Pang Juan would arrive at dusk.

tales.ja: [[p:孫臏]]は大木の皮を削って「[[p:龐涓]]この樹の下に死す」と書かせ、「火が見えたら一斉に射よ」と命じた。夜、着いた龐涓が字を読もうと松明をともした瞬間、矢が降り注いだ。龐涓は「ついに豎子の名を成さしめたか」と言って自ら首を刎ねた。
tales.en: [[p:孫臏|Sun Bin]] had the bark stripped from a great tree and wrote on it: "[[p:龐涓|Pang Juan]] dies beneath this tree", and told his archers to shoot as one when they saw a light. Pang Juan arrived in the dark and lit a torch to read the words — and the arrows fell. "So I have made that wretch famous," he said, and cut his own throat.

tales.ja: かつて二人は同じ師に学んだ。[[p:孫臏]]の才を妬んだ[[p:龐涓]]は、孫臏を罪に陥れて両足を断つ刑に処し、顔に入れ墨をさせた。孫臏は斉の使者の車にひそかに隠れて魏を逃れていた。
tales.en: The two had studied under the same master. Jealous of [[p:孫臏|Sun Bin]]'s gifts, [[p:龐涓|Pang Juan]] had him falsely accused, his feet cut off and his face tattooed; Sun Bin escaped Wei hidden in the carriage of a Qi envoy.

after.ja: 魏の太子申は捕らえられ、魏は戦国の初めの覇権を失った。斉の威王は東方の最強国となった。
after.en: The Wei crown prince Shen was captured and Wei lost the primacy it had held since the Warring States began. King Wei of Qi was master of the east.

deploy.ja: 上党を受け入れた趙に、秦は[[p:王齕]]の大軍を向けた。趙の老将[[p:廉頗]]は塁を固めて三年近く戦わず、秦の兵站を消耗させた。
deploy.en: Zhao accepted Shangdang, and Qin sent [[p:王齕|Wang He]] with a great army. The veteran [[p:廉頗|Lian Po]] built ramparts and would not fight for nearly three years, wearing down Qin's supply lines.

plan.ja: 秦の[[p:范雎]]は「秦が恐れるのは[[p:廉頗]]ではなく[[p:趙奢]]の子[[p:趙括]]だ」との噂を趙に流した。趙王は廉頗を退けて趙括を将とした。秦はひそかに[[p:白起]]を総大将に替え、偽って退いて趙括を塁の外へ誘い出し、二万五千の伏兵で退路を断ち、五千の騎兵で趙軍を二つに分けた。趙軍は四十六日間食を断たれ、互いに食らい合うほどになった。
plan.en: [[p:范雎|Fan Ju]] of Qin spread the word in Zhao that what Qin feared was not [[p:廉頗|Lian Po]] but [[p:趙括|Zhao Kuo]], son of [[p:趙奢|Zhao She]]. The King of Zhao replaced Lian Po with Zhao Kuo. Qin secretly made [[p:白起|Bai Qi]] its commander, feigned a retreat to draw Zhao Kuo out of his ramparts, cut his line of retreat with twenty-five thousand men and split the Zhao army in two with five thousand horse. Without food for forty-six days, the Zhao soldiers were reduced to eating one another.

tales.ja: [[p:趙括]]は兵書をそらんじ、議論では父の[[p:趙奢]]も言い負かしたが、父は「戦は死地なのに、括は易々と口にする。趙を破るのは括だ」と言った。趙括の母も王に「あの子を将にしないでください」と願い出ていた。
tales.en: [[p:趙括|Zhao Kuo]] knew the books of war by heart and could outargue even his father, but [[p:趙奢|Zhao She]] said: "War is a place of death, and Kuo talks of it lightly; if Zhao is ever broken, it will be by him." His mother too begged the king not to make him general.

tales.ja: [[p:趙括]]は自ら突撃して射殺され、降った四十万の兵は、二百四十人の少年を除いて穴埋めにされたと伝わる。後に[[p:白起]]は「長平の降卒を欺いて殺した。わたしが死ぬのは当然だ」と言って自害した。
tales.en: [[p:趙括|Zhao Kuo]] led a last charge and was shot down. The four hundred thousand who surrendered were buried alive, the records say, all but two hundred and forty boys. Years later, ordered to die, [[p:白起|Bai Qi]] said: "I deceived and killed the men who surrendered at Changping. I deserve to die."

after.ja: 趙は国の力のほとんどを失い、秦は邯鄲を囲んだが、[[p:信陵君]]らの救援で退いた。それでも戦国の力の均衡はここで決定的に秦へ傾いた。
after.en: Zhao lost most of its strength. Qin besieged Handan, and was driven off by [[p:信陵君|Lord Xinling]] and others — but the balance of the Warring States had tipped to Qin for good.

deploy.ja: 周の桓王は自ら中軍を率い、右軍に蔡・衛の兵、左軍に陳の兵を置いた。鄭は右に[[p:祭仲]]、左に高渠弥、中軍に荘公が立った。
deploy.en: King Huan of Zhou led his centre himself, with Cai and Wey on his right and Chen on his left. Zheng set [[p:祭仲|Zhai Zhong]] on its right, Gao Qumi on its left and Duke Zhuang in the centre.

plan.ja: 鄭の公子元は「陳は乱れていて戦う気がない。まず陳を討てば蔡・衛も崩れる」と説いた。鄭は戦車の間に歩兵を詰めて隙をなくした「魚麗の陣」で進み、陳・蔡・衛が崩れると、三方から王の中軍を挟み撃ちにした。
plan.en: Prince Yuan of Zheng argued that Chen, in turmoil at home, had no stomach for a fight: break it first, and Cai and Wey would follow. Zheng came on in the "fish-scale" order, foot soldiers packed between the chariots, and when Chen, Cai and Wey gave way it closed on the king's centre from three sides.

tales.ja: [[p:祝聃]]の矢が王の肩に当たった。祝聃が追おうとすると荘公は「君子は人を凌ぐことを望まない。まして天子を」と止め、その夜、[[p:祭仲]]を遣わして王と側近を見舞わせた。
tales.en: [[p:祝聃|Zhu Dan]]'s arrow struck the king in the shoulder. When he would have given chase, Duke Zhuang stopped him: "A gentleman does not wish to overbear others — still less the Son of Heaven." That night he sent [[p:祭仲|Zhai Zhong]] to ask after the king and his men.

after.ja: 王が諸侯の軍を率いて敗れたことで、周の権威は地に落ち、諸侯が自らの力で争う時代が始まった。
after.en: A king beaten at the head of the lords' armies: the authority of Zhou was broken, and an age of lords contending by their own strength began.

deploy.ja: 斉の大軍が魯に攻め入り、魯の荘公は長勺で迎え撃った。[[p:曹劌]]は「肉を食らう者は鄙し」と言って自ら願い出て、荘公の戦車に同乗した。
deploy.en: A great army of Qi invaded Lu, and Duke Zhuang met it at Changshao. [[p:曹劌|Cao Gui]] — "the meat-eaters are short-sighted" — asked to go and rode in the duke's own chariot.

plan.ja: 斉軍が太鼓を打って進むと、荘公も打とうとしたが、[[p:曹劌]]は止めた。斉が三度打ったところで「今です」と言い、魯軍は一度の太鼓で討って出て斉軍を破った。曹劌はすぐには追わせず、車から降りて斉の轍を見、横木に登って旗を望み、轍が乱れ旗が倒れているのを確かめてから追撃を許した。
plan.en: When the Qi drums sounded the advance, the duke wished to answer; [[p:曹劌|Cao Gui]] held him back. Only after Qi had drummed three times did he say "Now", and Lu went out at one drumbeat and broke Qi. Nor would he let them pursue until he had got down to look at the Qi wheel-ruts and climbed the crossbar to see their banners: ruts in disorder, banners down. Then the chase was given.

tales.ja: 「戦いは勇気である。一度の太鼓で気を起こし、二度で衰え、三度で尽きる。彼が尽きて我が満ちていたから勝ったのだ」と[[p:曹劌]]は語った。
tales.en: "Battle is courage," said [[p:曹劌|Cao Gui]]. "The first drum rouses it, the second dulls it, the third spends it. Theirs was spent and ours was full: so we won."

after.ja: 斉は同じ年の夏、宋とともに再び魯を攻めたが、乗丘でまた敗れた。
after.en: That summer Qi came again with Song, and was beaten again at Shengqiu.

deploy.ja: 飢饉の年に秦から穀物を受けながら、秦の飢饉には穀物を拒んだ晋に、秦の穆公は兵を向けた。晋の恵公は、鄭から贈られた小柄な馬に戦車を引かせて出た。
deploy.en: Jin had taken Qin's grain in its own famine and refused grain in Qin's; Duke Mu of Qin marched. Duke Hui of Jin went out behind a team of small horses, a gift from Zheng.

plan.ja: 乱戦のなか、晋の恵公の馬はぬかるみにはまって動けなくなった。慶鄭は呼ばれても助けに行かず、穆公を囲んでいた晋兵も恵公の救いに回ったため、穆公は逃れ、恵公は捕らえられた。
plan.en: In the melee Duke Hui's horses stuck fast in the mud. Qing Zheng, called to help, would not come; the Jin men who had surrounded Duke Mu broke off to save their own lord — so Duke Mu escaped, and Duke Hui was taken.

tales.ja: かつて穆公の馬を食べた岐山の野人三百人が、恩返しに駆けつけて穆公を救ったという (『史記』)。
tales.en: Three hundred hill-men of Mount Qi, who had once eaten Duke Mu's lost horse and been forgiven, came running to repay him and saved him, it is told (Shiji).

after.ja: 恵公の姉である穆公の夫人が喪服で子らと薪の上に立って命乞いをし、穆公は恵公を帰した。晋は河西の地を秦に差し出し、太子圉を人質に送った。
after.en: Duke Mu's wife — Duke Hui's sister — stood with her children on a pyre in mourning clothes to beg for her brother's life, and Duke Mu let him go home. Jin gave up the land west of the river and sent the heir Yu as hostage.

deploy.ja: 鄭を救うために楚が宋に兵を向け、宋の襄公は泓水のほとりで迎え撃った。宋軍は先に陣を整えて待っていた。
deploy.en: Chu marched on Song to relieve Zheng; Duke Xiang of Song met it on the River Hong, his army already drawn up and waiting.

plan.ja: 楚軍が川を渡りきらぬうちに、司馬子魚 ([[p:公子目夷]]) は「敵は多く我は少ない。渡りきらぬうちに撃ちましょう」と説いたが、襄公は許さなかった。渡りきって陣を整えぬうちにと再び説いても許さず、楚軍が陣を整えてから戦って大敗した。
plan.en: While Chu was still crossing, the marshal Ziyu (Prince Muyi) urged: "They are many and we are few — strike before they are across." The duke refused. Across but not yet formed — strike now; again he refused. Only when Chu stood in order did he fight, and he was crushed.

tales.ja: 襄公は「君子は傷ついた者を重ねて傷つけず、白髪の者を捕らえない。陣を成さぬ敵に太鼓は打たぬ」と言った。子魚は「君は戦を知らない」と嘆いた。「宋襄の仁」の故事である。
tales.en: "A gentleman does not wound the wounded twice, nor take the grey-haired prisoner, nor drum against an enemy not yet formed," said the duke. "My lord does not understand war," sighed Ziyu. Thus "the benevolence of Duke Xiang of Song".

after.ja: 襄公は股に受けた傷がもとで翌年没し、宋の覇業の夢は消えた。
after.en: The duke died the next year of the wound in his thigh, and Song's dream of leading the lords died with him.

deploy.ja: 喪中の晋は、鄭を襲いに出て引き返す秦軍を、殽山の険しい谷で待ち伏せた。晋の襄公は喪服を墨で黒く染めて出陣し、姜戎の兵も加わった。
deploy.en: Jin, in mourning, lay in wait in the steep gorges of Mount Xiao for the Qin army coming home from its failed raid on Zheng. Duke Xiang went to war in mourning clothes dyed black, with the Jiang Rong beside him.

plan.ja: 細い谷道に入った秦軍を、晋と姜戎が前後から塞いで討った。秦軍は「一頭の馬も一つの車輪も帰らなかった」と言われるほど全滅し、三人の将は捕らえられた。
plan.en: Jin and the Jiang Rong closed the narrow gorge front and rear. Not a horse nor a wheel went home, it was said, and the three Qin commanders were taken.

tales.ja: 出陣の日、老臣[[p:蹇叔]]は息子の[[p:西乞術]]・[[p:白乙丙]]に「お前たちは必ず殽で死ぬ。私はそこで骨を拾おう」と泣いて送り出し、穆公に「お前の墓の木はもう一抱えにもなろう」と罵られた。
tales.en: On the day the army left, old [[p:蹇叔|Jian Shu]] wept as he saw off his sons: "You will die at Xiao, and there I shall gather your bones." Duke Mu cursed him: "The trees on your grave would already be an armspan thick."

after.ja: 捕らえられた三将は、文公の夫人 (秦の娘) のとりなしで帰された。穆公は喪服で郊外まで出迎え、「私が[[p:蹇叔]]の言葉を聞かなかったのが悪い」と自らを責め、[[p:孟明視]]を用い続けた。
after.en: At the plea of Duke Wen's widow, a daughter of Qin, the three were sent home. Duke Mu met them outside the city in mourning — "The fault is mine, for not heeding [[p:蹇叔|Jian Shu]]" — and kept [[p:孟明視|Meng Mingshi]] in command.

deploy.ja: 魯・衛の求めに応じて晋は八百乗の戦車を出し、中軍を[[p:郤克]]が率いた。斉の頃公は「この敵を滅ぼしてから朝食にしよう」と言い、馬に鎧も着けずに駆け出した。
deploy.en: At the call of Lu and Wey, Jin sent eight hundred chariots under [[p:郤克|Xi Ke]]. Duke Qing of Qi cried, "Let us finish them off, then breakfast," and charged without armour on his horses.

plan.ja: [[p:郤克]]は矢に当たって血が靴まで流れても太鼓を打ち続け、御者の解張は折れた矢で手を射抜かれたまま手綱を握り続けた。晋軍は斉軍を三度めぐるほど追いまくった。
plan.en: [[p:郤克|Xi Ke]], hit by an arrow, kept beating the drum with the blood running into his shoes; his driver Xie Zhang held the reins with an arrow through his hand. Jin drove Qi three times round the hill of Huabuzhu.

tales.ja: [[p:韓厥]]に追いつかれた頃公は、車右の逢丑父と席を入れ替え、水を汲みに行かされたふりをして逃れた。身代わりの逢丑父は[[p:郤克]]に「君に代わって難を引き受ける者を殺せば不吉」と言われ、許された。
tales.en: Overtaken by [[p:韓厥|Han Jue]], Duke Qing changed places with his spearman Feng Choufu and escaped as if sent to fetch water. [[p:郤克|Xi Ke]] spared the stand-in: "To kill a man who takes his lord's danger on himself is unlucky."

after.ja: 斉は袁婁で晋と盟を結び、奪っていた汶陽の田を魯に返した。
after.en: Qi swore peace with Jin at Yuanlou and gave back the fields of Wenyang it had taken from Lu.

deploy.ja: 鄭が楚についたので晋は鄭を討ち、楚の共王が救いに来た。楚軍は朝早く晋の陣に迫り、晋は陣中の井戸を埋め竈を壊して場所を作って布陣した。
deploy.en: Zheng had gone over to Chu, so Jin attacked it, and King Gong of Chu came to its aid. Chu pressed close to the Jin camp at dawn; Jin filled in its wells and flattened its stoves to make room to form up.

plan.ja: 楚から亡命した苗賁皇は「楚の精兵は中軍の王の親兵だけ。左右を破ってから三方で王を攻めよ」と説いた。晋軍が左右を崩すと、晋の呂錡の矢が共王の目を射た。
plan.en: Miao Fenhuang, an exile from Chu, told Jin that Chu's best men were only the king's guard in the centre: break the wings, then close on the king from three sides. Jin broke the wings, and an arrow of Lü Qi struck King Gong in the eye.

tales.ja: その夜、楚の共王は軍議のため[[p:子反]]を呼んだが、子反は酒に酔って起きられなかった。王は「天が楚を敗ったのだ」と言って夜のうちに兵を引いた。
tales.en: That night King Gong sent for [[p:子反|Zifan]] to plan the next day; Zifan was too drunk to rise. "Heaven has beaten Chu," said the king, and withdrew in the dark.

after.ja: [[p:子反]]は敗戦の責めを負って自ら命を絶った。勝った晋の厲公は驕り、のちに臣下に殺される。
after.en: [[p:子反|Zifan]] took the blame and killed himself. Duke Li of Jin, proud in victory, would later be killed by his own ministers.

deploy.ja: 越王[[p:允常]]の死を聞いて、呉の[[p:闔閭]]は越に攻め入った。立ったばかりの越王[[p:句践]]は檇李で迎え撃った。
deploy.en: Hearing that King [[p:允常|Yunchang]] of Yue had died, [[p:闔閭|Helü]] of Wu invaded. The new king, [[p:句践|Goujian]], met him at Zuili.

plan.ja: [[p:句践]]は決死の兵に二度突っ込ませても呉の陣は乱れなかった。そこで罪人を三列に並ばせ、「軍令を犯した。刑を逃れず死ぬ」と叫ばせて次々に自ら首を刎ねさせた。呉兵が呆然と見入るところを越軍が突き、呉は大敗した。
plan.en: Twice [[p:句践|Goujian]] sent picked men to charge and twice the Wu line held. Then he set condemned men in three ranks before it; crying that they had broken the army's law and would not escape the penalty, they cut their own throats one after another. While Wu stared, Yue struck, and Wu was routed.

tales.ja: 越の霊姑浮の戈が[[p:闔閭]]の足の指を切り落とし、闔閭はその傷がもとで陘で没した。
tales.en: Ling Gufu of Yue cut off [[p:闔閭|Helü]]'s big toe with his dagger-axe; the wound killed him at Xing.

after.ja: 子の[[p:夫差]]は庭に人を立たせ、出入りのたびに「夫差、越王が汝の父を殺したのを忘れたか」と言わせて、復讐を誓った。
after.en: His son [[p:夫差|Fuchai]] set a man in the courtyard to call out each time he passed: "Fuchai, have you forgotten that the King of Yue killed your father?"

deploy.ja: 呉が兵を鍛えていると聞いた[[p:句践]]は、[[p:范蠡]]の諫めを聞かずに先に攻め込んだ。[[p:夫差]]は精兵を挙げて太湖の夫椒で迎え撃った。
deploy.en: Hearing that Wu was training for war, [[p:句践|Goujian]] struck first, against [[p:范蠡|Fan Li]]'s advice. [[p:夫差|Fuchai]] met him with his best troops at Fujiao on Lake Tai.

plan.ja: 復讐に燃える呉軍は越軍を打ち破り、[[p:句践]]は五千の兵とともに会稽山に追い詰められた。
plan.en: Burning for revenge, Wu smashed the Yue army, and [[p:句践|Goujian]] was driven up Mount Kuaiji with five thousand men.

tales.ja: [[p:文種]]は呉の宰相[[p:伯嚭]]に美女と宝を贈って和を取りなさせた。[[p:伍子胥]]は「今越を滅ぼさなければ、二十年のうちに呉は沼になる」と説いたが、[[p:夫差]]は聞かなかった。
tales.en: [[p:文種|Wen Zhong]] sent beauties and treasure to [[p:伯嚭|Bo Pi]], Wu's chief minister, to speak for peace. "Destroy Yue now," urged [[p:伍子胥|Wu Zixu]], "or within twenty years Wu will be a swamp." [[p:夫差|Fuchai]] did not listen.

after.ja: [[p:句践]]は呉に降って自ら[[p:夫差]]の臣となり、三年仕えて帰国を許された。
after.en: [[p:句践|Goujian]] surrendered, served [[p:夫差|Fuchai]] as his subject for three years, and was allowed home.

deploy.ja: 呉の[[p:夫差]]は魯と結んで斉に攻め入った。斉は[[p:国書]]が中軍を率いた。
deploy.en: [[p:夫差|Fuchai]] of Wu, allied with Lu, invaded Qi; [[p:国書|Guo Shu]] led the Qi centre.

plan.ja: 斉の将たちは死を覚悟し、公孫夏は葬送の歌を歌わせ、陳子行は口に含ませる玉を用意させた。戦いは呉の大勝に終わり、[[p:国書]]は討たれ、甲冑を積んだ戦車八百乗が呉の手に落ちた。
plan.en: The Qi commanders went out expecting to die: [[p:公孫喜|Gongsun Xi]]a had his men sing the funeral song, Chen Zixing had the jade made ready for his mouth. Wu won outright; [[p:国書|Guo Shu]] was killed and eight hundred chariots with their armour were taken.

tales.ja: 勝ち誇る[[p:夫差]]に、[[p:伍子胥]]は「越は腹の病、斉は皮膚の病にすぎぬ」と諫め、剣を賜って死んだ。
tales.en: As [[p:夫差|Fuchai]] gloried in the victory [[p:伍子胥|Wu Zixu]] warned him that Yue was a disease of the belly, Qi only of the skin — and was sent a sword to die by.

after.ja: 呉は中原へ進む力を得たが、その背後で越が力を蓄えていた。
after.en: Wu had the strength to reach for the central plain — while behind it Yue gathered its own.

deploy.ja: 魏の[[p:龐涓]]が趙の都邯鄲を囲み、趙は斉に救いを求めた。斉は[[p:田忌]]を将、[[p:孫臏]]を軍師とした。孫臏は足を切られた身であったので、幌のある車に乗って策を練った。
deploy.en: [[p:龐涓|Pang Juan]] of Wei besieged Handan, and Zhao begged Qi for help. Qi made [[p:田忌|Tian Ji]] general and [[p:孫臏|Sun Bin]] his strategist — Sun Bin, whose feet had been cut, planning from a covered carriage.

plan.ja: [[p:田忌]]が邯鄲へ向かおうとすると、[[p:孫臏]]は「もつれた糸は拳で叩いても解けない。手薄な所を突けば相手は自ずから退く」と説き、魏の都大梁を突かせた。慌てて引き返した魏軍を、斉軍は桂陵で待ち伏せて破った (囲魏救趙)。
plan.en: [[p:田忌|Tian Ji]] would have marched straight to Handan. "You don't untangle a knot by punching it," said [[p:孫臏|Sun Bin]]: strike where Wei is empty, and it will let go of its own accord. Qi made for Wei's capital Daliang; the Wei army hurried home and was ambushed and beaten at Guiling — "besiege Wei to save Zhao".

after.ja: 魏は邯鄲を落としたものの、二年後に趙へ返して漳水のほとりで盟を結んだ。
after.en: Wei had taken Handan, but two years later handed it back and swore peace with Zhao by the River Zhang.

deploy.ja: 韓・魏の連合軍が伊水の狭い谷 (伊闕) に陣を敷き、秦は新たに将となった[[p:白起]]を送った。韓・魏はどちらも相手に先陣を譲りあって動かなかった。
deploy.en: Han and Wei camped together in the narrow gorge of the Yi, and Qin sent [[p:白起|Bai Qi]], newly in command. Each ally waited for the other to lead, and neither moved.

plan.ja: [[p:白起]]は少数の兵で韓軍を引きつけておき、主力で魏軍を急襲した。魏が崩れると、取り残された韓軍も崩れた。
plan.en: [[p:白起|Bai Qi]] held the Han army with a small force and fell on Wei with his main strength. Wei broke, and Han, left alone, broke after it.

after.ja: 首を斬ること二十四万、魏の将[[p:公孫喜]]は捕らえられ、五つの城が落ちた。[[p:白起]]の名は天下に轟いた。
after.en: Two hundred and forty thousand heads were taken, the Wei general [[p:公孫喜|Gongsun Xi]] captured and five cities taken. [[p:白起|Bai Qi]]'s name rang through the world.

deploy.ja: 燕の[[p:楽毅]]は秦・韓・趙・魏の兵をあわせた五国の軍を率いて斉に攻め入った。斉の湣王は国中の兵を済水の西に集めて迎え撃った。
deploy.en: [[p:楽毅|Yue Yi]] of Yan led the armies of five states — Yan with Qin, Han, Zhao and Wei — into Qi. King Min massed every soldier he had west of the River Ji.

plan.ja: 驕った湣王に背を向けていた斉兵は戦意に乏しく、済西で大敗した。[[p:楽毅]]は他国の兵を帰し、燕軍だけで逃げる斉軍を追って都臨淄に入った。
plan.en: The Qi soldiers had little heart for a king who had turned the world against him, and broke at Jixi. [[p:楽毅|Yue Yi]] sent the other armies home and with Yan's alone chased the fleeing Qi into Linzi.

after.ja: [[p:楽毅]]は半年のうちに斉の七十余城を落とし、斉に残ったのは莒と即墨だけであった。
after.en: Within half a year [[p:楽毅|Yue Yi]] had taken over seventy cities of Qi; only Ju and Jimo held out.

deploy.ja: 即墨を五年守る[[p:田単]]は、燕の新しい王に[[p:楽毅]]を疑わせる噂を流させた。楽毅は趙へ逃れ、凡庸な[[p:騎劫]]が代わって燕の将となった。
deploy.en: [[p:田単|Tian Dan]], five years holding Jimo, spread rumours that set Yan's new king against [[p:楽毅|Yue Yi]]. Yue Yi fled to Zhao, and the dull [[p:騎劫|Qi Jie]] took his command.

plan.ja: [[p:田単]]は千頭の牛に五色の竜を描いた絹を着せ、角に刃を縛り、尾に油を染ませた葦を結んで火をつけ、夜に城壁の穴から燕の陣へ放った。後ろから五千の兵が続き、城中の老人や子供は銅器を打ち鳴らした。燕軍は総崩れになり、[[p:騎劫]]は討たれた。
plan.en: [[p:田単|Tian Dan]] dressed a thousand oxen in silk painted with five-coloured dragons, tied blades to their horns and oil-soaked reeds to their tails, set the reeds alight and drove them by night through holes in the wall into the Yan camp. Five thousand men ran behind, while the old and young of the city beat on bronze. Yan broke, and [[p:騎劫|Qi Jie]] was killed.

tales.ja: [[p:田単]]はわざと「燕兵が捕虜の鼻を削ぎ、城外の墓をあばくのを斉人は恐れている」と噂を流し、燕軍がそのとおりにするのを見た城中の斉人は怒りに燃えた。
tales.en: [[p:田単|Tian Dan]] let it be known that the people of Jimo dreaded nothing more than Yan cutting off their captives' noses and digging up their graves — and when Yan did just that, the city burned with rage.

after.ja: [[p:田単]]は勢いに乗って七十余城をすべて取り戻し、莒にいた襄王を臨淄に迎えた。
after.en: Riding the tide [[p:田単|Tian Dan]] won back all seventy cities and brought [[p:燕王喜|King Xi]]ang from Ju to Linzi.

deploy.ja: 秦が韓を攻めて閼与を囲み、趙は救援を議した。[[p:廉頗]]も楽乗も「道は遠く険しい」と首を振ったが、[[p:趙奢]]だけが「狭い道の戦いは穴の中の鼠の闘い、勇ましい方が勝つ」と言って将となった。
deploy.en: Qin besieged Eyu, and Zhao debated a relief. [[p:廉頗|Lian Po]] and Yue Cheng shook their heads — the road was long and steep; only [[p:趙奢|Zhao She]] said a fight in a narrow pass is two rats in a hole, and the braver wins. He was given the command.

plan.ja: [[p:趙奢]]は都から三十里で陣を止めて二十八日動かず、「軍のことで諫める者は死罪」として秦の間者も帰した。秦が油断したと見るや二日一夜で閼与に至り、許歴の進言で北の山を先に取って、攻め上る秦軍を破った。
plan.en: [[p:趙奢|Zhao She]] halted thirty li out and did not stir for twenty-eight days, death to any who argued, and let a Qin spy go home to report it. When Qin was off its guard he reached Eyu in two days and a night, took the northern hill first on Xu Li's advice, and broke the Qin army as it climbed.

after.ja: 趙の[[p:恵文王]]は[[p:趙奢]]を馬服君に封じ、[[p:廉頗]]・[[p:藺相如]]と並ぶ位につけた。
after.en: [[p:恵文王|King Huiwen]] of Zhao made [[p:趙奢|Zhao She]] Lord of Mafu, equal in rank to [[p:廉頗|Lian Po]] and [[p:藺相如|Lin Xiangru]].

deploy.ja: 秦の若い将[[p:李信]]と[[p:蒙恬]]は二十万で楚に攻め入り、それぞれ平輿と寝を破った。
deploy.en: Young [[p:李信|Li Xin]] and [[p:蒙恬|Meng Tian]] of Qin invaded Chu with two hundred thousand and took Pingyu and Qin.

plan.ja: 勝ちに乗った[[p:李信]]が城父で[[p:蒙恬]]と合流しようとしたところを、[[p:項燕]]の楚軍が三日三晩休まず追い、二つの陣を破り、七人の都尉を討ち取った。
plan.en: As [[p:李信|Li Xin]], flushed with success, made to join [[p:蒙恬|Meng Tian]] at Chengfu, [[p:項燕|Xiang Yan]]'s army followed him three days and nights without rest, broke two of his camps and killed seven of his colonels.

after.ja: 秦王は自ら頻陽に退いていた[[p:王翦]]を訪ねて詫び、六十万の兵を委ねた。
after.en: The King of Qin went himself to [[p:王翦|Wang Jian]] in retirement at Pinyang, apologised, and gave him six hundred thousand men.

name.en: the battle of south of Qi

deploy.ja: [[p:王翦]]は六十万を率いて楚に入ったが、砦を固めて戦わず、兵に湯浴みさせ、よく食べさせて、自らも兵と同じものを食べた。
deploy.en: [[p:王翦|Wang Jian]] led six hundred thousand into Chu — and built forts and would not fight; he had his men bathe and eat well, and ate what they ate.

plan.ja: しばらくして兵たちが石投げや幅跳びで遊んでいると聞くと、[[p:王翦]]は「使える」と言った。挑んでも出てこない秦軍に楚軍が東へ引き揚げ始めると、王翦は全軍で追って蘄の南で楚軍を破った。
plan.en: When he heard his men were playing at stone-throwing and long-jumping, he said "Now they are ready." Chu, unable to draw him out, began to move off east; [[p:王翦|Wang Jian]] went after it with everything and broke it south of Qi.

tales.ja: 出陣の前、[[p:王翦]]はしきりに良い田や屋敷を王にねだった。「王は疑い深い。国中の兵を預かる者が子孫のための財を求めれば、王は安心する」と王翦は語った。
tales.en: Before setting out [[p:王翦|Wang Jian]] kept asking the king for good fields and houses. "The king is suspicious," he explained. "A man trusted with every soldier in the realm who asks for wealth for his grandchildren is a man the king need not fear."

after.ja: [[p:項燕]]は敗れて死に、翌年楚王[[p:負芻]]は捕らえられて楚は滅んだ。
after.en: [[p:項燕|Xiang Yan]] was beaten and died, and the next year King [[p:負芻|Fuchu]] was taken and Chu was no more.

name.en: the campaign of the East Gate

terms.ja: 五日の囲みの後、諸侯の軍は得るところなく引き揚げた。
terms.en: After five days' siege the lords' armies went home with nothing.

terms.ja: 王は兵を引いた。鄭の荘公は夜のうちに[[p:祭仲]]を遣わして王と側近を見舞った。
terms.en: The king withdrew. That night Duke Zhuang of Zheng sent [[p:祭仲|Zhai Zhong]] to ask after him and his men.

terms.ja: 斉軍は退いた。夏、斉は宋とともに再び魯を攻めたが、乗丘でまた敗れた。
terms.en: Qi fell back; that summer it came again with Song and was beaten again at Shengqiu.

name.en: Duke Huan of Qi's campaign against the Mountain Rong

terms.ja: 山戎は北へ退いた。燕の荘公が桓公を見送って斉の領内まで入ると、桓公は「諸侯を見送るのは国境まで」と、荘公が踏み入った土地を燕に与えた。
terms.en: The Mountain Rong fell back north. When Duke Zhuang of Yan, seeing Duke Huan off, crossed into Qi, Huan gave him the ground he had stood on: a lord sees another only to his own border.

terms.ja: 楚の屈完が斉の陣に来て、召陵で盟を結んだ。楚は周への貢ぎ物を約した。
terms.en: Qu Wan of Chu came to the Qi camp and they swore a covenant at Zhaoling; Chu promised its tribute to Zhou.

terms.ja: 捕らえられた晋の恵公は、秦の夫人 (恵公の姉) の嘆願で帰された。晋は河西の地を秦に差し出し、太子圉を人質に送った。
terms.en: The captive Duke Hui was sent home at the plea of Qin's duchess, his sister. Jin gave up the land west of the river and sent the heir Yu as hostage.

terms.ja: 宋の襄公は股の傷がもとで翌年没した。
terms.en: Duke Xiang of Song died the next year of the wound in his thigh.

terms.ja: 楚は宋の囲みを解いて退いた。晋は践土で周王を迎えて諸侯と盟を結び、文公は覇者となった。
terms.en: Chu lifted the siege of Song and withdrew. At Jiantu Jin received the king of Zhou and bound the lords in covenant; Duke Wen was hegemon.

terms.ja: 捕らえられた秦の三将は、文公の夫人のとりなしで帰された。
terms.en: The three captive Qin commanders were sent home at the plea of Duke Wen's widow.

terms.ja: 晋は河の北へ退き、鄭は楚に従った。
terms.en: Jin fell back north of the river and Zheng followed Chu.

terms.ja: 楚は兵を三十里退いて宋と盟を結び、[[p:華元]]は人質として楚に入った。
terms.en: Chu drew back thirty li and swore peace with Song; [[p:華元|Hua Yuan]] went to Chu as hostage.

terms.ja: 斉は袁婁で晋と盟を結び、汶陽の田を魯に返した。
terms.en: Qi swore peace with Jin at Yuanlou and gave the fields of Wenyang back to Lu.

terms.ja: 晋と諸侯の軍は秦を涇水まで追い、引き揚げた。
terms.en: Jin and the lords chased Qin to the River Jing and went home.

terms.ja: 楚の[[p:子反]]は責めを負って自害し、鄭はなお楚に従った。
terms.en: [[p:子反|Zifan]] of Chu took the blame and killed himself; Zheng stayed with Chu.

terms.ja: 斉の霊公が没したと聞くと、晋の士匄は「喪に乗じて攻めるのは礼にあらず」と兵を返した。
terms.en: When word came that Duke Ling of Qi had died, Shi Gai of Jin turned back: to strike a house in mourning was not right.

terms.ja: [[p:申包胥]]が秦の庭で七日七晩泣き続けて得た秦の援軍が来ると、呉は郢を去った。
terms.en: When the army of Qin came — won by [[p:申包胥|Shen Baoxu]], who wept seven days and nights in the Qin court — Wu left Ying.

terms.ja: 呉王[[p:闔閭]]は足の傷がもとで陘で没し、子の[[p:夫差]]が復讐を誓った。
terms.en: King [[p:闔閭|Helü]] of Wu died of his wound at Xing, and his son [[p:夫差|Fuchai]] swore revenge.

terms.ja: [[p:句践]]は会稽で降り、自ら[[p:夫差]]の臣となった。
terms.en: [[p:句践|Goujian]] surrendered at Kuaiji and became [[p:夫差|Fuchai]]'s subject.

terms.ja: 呉は艾陵で斉の大軍を破り、斉は呉に従った。
terms.en: Wu broke the great army of Qi at Ailing, and Qi bowed to Wu.

terms.ja: 姑蘇は三年の囲みの末に落ち、呉王[[p:夫差]]は「子胥に合わせる顔がない」と顔を布で覆って自害した。呉は越に併せられた。
terms.en: Gusu fell after a three-year siege. King [[p:夫差|Fuchai]] of Wu covered his face — "I cannot face [[p:伍子胥|Wu Zixu]]" — and killed himself; Wu was joined to Yue.

terms.ja: 周の顕王は秦の献公に礼服を贈って勝利を祝った。
terms.en: [[p:燕王喜|King Xi]]an of Zhou sent robes of honour to Duke Xian of Qin for his victory.

terms.ja: 魏は邯鄲を落としたが、のちに趙へ返して漳水のほとりで盟を結んだ。
terms.en: Wei had taken Handan, but later gave it back and swore peace with Zhao by the Zhang.

terms.ja: 魏は太子申と[[p:龐涓]]を失い、斉に和を請うた。
terms.en: Wei, having lost the crown prince Shen and [[p:龐涓|Pang Juan]], sued Qi for peace.

name.en: the five states' war on Qin

terms.ja: 函谷関で退けられ、修魚で敗れた韓・趙は秦に和を求めた。
terms.en: Thrown back at the Hangu Pass and beaten at Xiuyu, Han and Zhao sought peace with Qin.

name.ja: 子之の乱と斉の燕侵攻
name.en: the troubles of Zizhi and Qi's invasion of Yan

terms.ja: 諸侯の非難と燕人の抵抗に、斉軍は燕から引き揚げた。燕は昭王を立て、後に[[p:楽毅]]を用いて斉に報いる。
terms.en: Under the censure of the lords and the resistance of the people of Yan, Qi withdrew. Yan enthroned King Zhao, who would later repay Qi through [[p:楽毅|Yue Yi]].

terms.ja: 楚は漢中を失い、韓・魏に背後を突かれて兵を退いた。
terms.en: Chu lost Hanzhong, and with Han and Wei at its back pulled its army home.

name.en: Qi, Han and Wei's war on Qin

terms.ja: 秦は韓に河外と武遂を、魏に河外と封陵を返して和を結んだ。
terms.en: Qin made peace, giving Han back Hewai and Wusui and Wei Hewai and Fengling.

terms.ja: 韓・魏は主力を失い、秦の東進を阻む力を失った。
terms.en: Han and Wei had lost their armies, and with them the power to stop Qin's march east.

terms.ja: [[p:田単]]は七十余城をすべて取り戻し、襄王を臨淄に迎えた。
terms.en: [[p:田単|Tian Dan]] won back all seventy cities and brought [[p:燕王喜|King Xi]]ang home to Linzi.

terms.ja: 趙の[[p:恵文王]]は[[p:趙奢]]を馬服君に封じた。
terms.en: [[p:恵文王|King Huiwen]] of Zhao made [[p:趙奢|Zhao She]] Lord of Mafu.

terms.ja: 長平の後、秦は邯鄲を囲んだが、魏の[[p:信陵君]]と楚の[[p:春申君]]の救援に破れて退いた。趙は持ちこたえたが、国力は戻らなかった。
terms.en: After Changping Qin besieged Handan, but was beaten off by the relief armies of [[p:信陵君|Lord Xinling]] of Wei and [[p:春申君|Lord Chunshen]] of Chu. Zhao survived, but never recovered its strength.

terms.ja: [[p:廉頗]]は燕の都を囲み、燕は城を割いて和を請うた。
terms.en: [[p:廉頗|Lian Po]] besieged the Yan capital, and Yan ceded cities for peace.

terms.ja: 秦軍は函谷関の内に退いた。秦は[[p:信陵君]]を讒し、魏王は信陵君から兵を取り上げた。
terms.en: Qin fell back behind the Hangu Pass — and slandered [[p:信陵君|Lord Xinling]] until the King of Wei took his army from him.

terms.ja: 五国の軍は散り、楚は都を寿春へ移した。最後の合従であった。
terms.en: The five armies scattered and Chu moved its capital to Shouchun. It was the last alliance against Qin.

terms.ja: 邯鄲は落ち、趙王遷は捕らえられた。公子嘉は代へ逃れて代王を称した。
terms.en: Handan fell and King Qian of Zhao was taken; Prince Jia fled to Dai and called himself its king.

terms.ja: [[p:項燕]]は敗れて死に、楚王[[p:負芻]]は捕らえられた。楚は滅んだ。
terms.en: [[p:項燕|Xiang Yan]] was beaten and died, King [[p:負芻|Fuchu]] was taken, and Chu was no more.

terms.ja: 遼東に逃れた[[p:燕王喜]]は捕らえられ、燕は滅んだ。
terms.en: [[p:燕王喜|King Xi]] of Yan, fled to Liaodong, was taken, and Yan was no more.

body.ja:
前307年、趙の[[p:武霊王]]は「胡服騎射」を命じた。胡服とは北方の遊牧の民の服である。筒袖の短い上着、馬にまたがれるズボン (袴)、革の長靴、帯を留める金具。中原の貴族は裾の長い衣を着て、戦では戦車の上に立って戦っていた。裾を引きずる衣では馬に乗れない。王は、服から変えなければ騎兵は生まれないと考えた。

反対は激しかった。服は礼であり、礼こそが中華と夷狄を分けるもの、というのが貴族たちの考えであった。王の叔父の[[p:公子成]]は病と称して朝廷に出てこなかった。王は自ら叔父の屋敷を訪ね、「服は着る者の便のため、礼は事を成すためのものです。聖人は国を利するなら古いしきたりにこだわりません」と説いた。翌日、公子成は胡服を着て朝廷に現れた。

なぜ騎兵だったのか。趙は北と西で林胡・楼煩などの遊牧の民と境を接していた。彼らは馬上から弓を射て、戦車の入れない山や草原を自在に駆け回る。戦車は平らな土地でしか使えず、一台に馬四頭と兵三人が要る。騎兵なら一頭に一人、山でも谷でも行ける。武霊王は、敵の戦い方そのものを取り入れたのである。

効き目はすぐに現れた。趙は林胡・楼煩を討って雲中・雁門・代の郡を置き、長年の敵であった中山国を滅ぼした。降った楼煩の騎兵も自軍に組み入れ、趙の北辺の騎兵は戦国で最も強いと言われるようになった。のちに匈奴の大軍を破った名将[[p:李牧]]も、この騎兵を率いて戦っている。

王の最期は悲劇であった。王は位を若い子 ([[p:恵文王]]) に譲って自らは「主父」と名乗り、なお軍を率い続けた。ところが、廃した長子の反乱に巻き込まれ、沙丘の離宮を三か月余り囲まれて、雀の雛まで食べ尽くして餓死したという。

胡服の影響は戦場の外にも残った。ズボンと長靴、帯の留め金 (帯鉤) はやがて中国の兵の普通の装いとなり、騎兵は秦と漢の軍の柱となっていく。「胡服騎射」は、伝統より実利を選んだ改革の代名詞として、今も語られている。
body.en:
In 307 BC [[p:武霊王|King Wuling]] of Zhao ordered "barbarian dress and mounted archery". The "barbarian dress" was the clothing of the northern herders: a short jacket with narrow sleeves, trousers a man could sit a horse in, leather boots and a belt hook. The nobles of the Central Plain wore long robes and fought standing in chariots — and no one can ride in a robe that trails on the ground. Without a change of clothes, the king reasoned, there would be no cavalry.

The opposition was fierce. Dress was ritual, said the nobles, and ritual was what set the civilised apart from the barbarians. The king's uncle, [[p:公子成|Prince Cheng]], pleaded illness and stayed away from court. The king went to his house himself: "Clothes are for the convenience of those who wear them; rites are for getting things done. A sage does not cling to old custom when the state can gain by changing it." The next day Prince Cheng came to court in trousers.

Why horsemen? To the north and west Zhao bordered herding peoples such as the Linhu and the Loufan, who shot from horseback and ranged over mountains and grassland where no chariot could go. A chariot needs flat ground, four horses and three men; a horseman needs one horse and goes anywhere. King Wuling simply took over his enemies' way of fighting.

It worked at once. Zhao struck the Linhu and Loufan, set up the commanderies of Yunzhong, Yanmen and Dai, and destroyed its old enemy, the state of Zhongshan. The Loufan horsemen who surrendered were taken into the army, and the cavalry of Zhao's northern frontier came to be thought the best of the Warring States. [[p:李牧|Li Mu]], who later crushed a great Xiongnu army, led these horsemen.

The king's end was tragic. He handed the throne to a young son ([[p:恵文王|King Huiwen]]), styled himself "the Lord Father" and went on leading armies — until he was caught up in the revolt of the elder son he had set aside, besieged in the palace at Shaqiu for more than three months, and starved to death after eating even the sparrow chicks in the eaves.

The change outlived him. Trousers, boots and belt hooks became the ordinary wear of Chinese soldiers, and cavalry became a pillar of the armies of Qin and Han. "Barbarian dress and mounted archery" is still the byword for a reform that put use before tradition.

title.en: The chariots of the Spring and Autumn

body.ja:
春秋の戦いの主役は、二頭または四頭の馬が引く二輪の戦車であった。車の上には三人が乗る。左に弓を持つ車左、右に戈 (ほこ) を持つ車右、中央で手綱を取る御者。車の後ろには数十人の歩兵が従い、戦車一台とその歩兵が一つの単位となった。

国の力は戦車の数で数えられた。「千乗の国」「万乗の君」という言葉は、戦車を千台、一万台出せる国、という意味である。城濮の戦いで晋が出した戦車は七百乗であった。

戦車の戦いには礼があった。整列を待たずに攻めない、逃げる敵を深追いしない、傷ついた者を重ねて傷つけない。泓水の戦い (前638年) で、宋の襄公は楚軍が河を渡りきり陣を整えるまで攻撃を待ち、大敗して自らも腿に傷を負い、翌年死んだ。後世「宋襄の仁」として笑われる話である。邲の戦いでは、楚兵が溝にはまった晋の戦車に抜け出し方を教えてやったという。

戦車は平地でしか力を出せない。山がちな北の地で狄と戦った晋の軍では、前541年、魏舒の進言で兵を車から降ろして歩兵の隊列を組ませ (「車を毀ちて行と為す」)、大原で狄を破った。戦国時代になると、歩兵の大軍と騎兵、そして弩が戦場を支配し、戦車はしだいに指揮官の乗り物となっていく。

戦車と弓の術は国から国へ伝わった。楚から晋へ亡命した[[p:巫臣]]は、晋の命で南の呉に渡り、戦車の御し方と陣の組み方を教えた。それまで舟と歩兵で戦っていた呉はこうして中原の戦い方を身につけ、八十年ほど後には楚の都に攻め入ることになる。
body.en:
The decisive arm of Spring and Autumn warfare was the two-wheeled chariot drawn by two or four horses. Three men rode in it: an archer on the left, a man with a dagger-axe on the right, and the driver in the middle. Behind came a few dozen foot soldiers; a chariot and its men made one unit.

A state's power was counted in chariots. "A state of a thousand chariots", "a lord of ten thousand chariots" meant one that could field that many. At Chengpu, Jin put seven hundred chariots in the field.

Chariot warfare had its courtesies: no attack before the enemy had formed up, no long pursuit of the fleeing, no second wound to the wounded. At the Hong river in 638 BC Duke Xiang of Song waited for the Chu army to cross and form its lines before attacking; he was routed, took a wound in the thigh and died the next year — "the benevolence of Duke Xiang" became a byword for folly. At Bi, Chu soldiers showed Jin charioteers stuck in a ditch how to get out.

Chariots need flat ground. Fighting the Di in the hills of the north in 541 BC, a Jin army on Wei Shu's advice broke up its chariots and formed its men into infantry files, and won at Dayuan. By the Warring States, masses of infantry, cavalry and the crossbow ruled the battlefield, and the chariot became a commander's vehicle.

The art of chariot and bow passed from state to state. Wuchen, an exile from Chu in Jin, was sent south to Wu to teach it how to drive chariots and draw up battle lines. Wu, which had fought with boats and foot soldiers, learned the ways of the Central Plain — and some eighty years later stormed the capital of Chu.

body.ja:
弩は、引き絞った弦を引き金の仕掛け (懸刀) で留めておき、狙いを定めてから放つ弓である。弓のように腕の力で引いたまま狙う必要がないので、力の弱い兵でも短い訓練で使え、強い弓よりも遠くへ、鎧を貫くほどの力で射ることができた。

戦国時代、弩は歩兵の主な武器となった。「天下の強い弓と弩はみな韓から出る」と言われ、韓の弩は六百歩先まで届いたという (遊説家[[p:蘇秦]]の言葉として伝わる)。青銅で精密に鋳た引き金の部品は形がそろい、壊れても取り替えることができた。

馬陵の戦いで[[p:孫臏]]は一万の弩兵を道の両側に伏せ、[[p:龐涓]]の軍を一斉の射撃で崩した。弩は隊列で一斉に放つときに最も力を発揮する。前の列が撃つ間に後ろの列が弦を張る、交代で撃つ工夫もされた。

始皇帝陵の兵馬俑には、ひざまずいて弩を構える兵の像が並んでいる。漢の時代には、足で弦を踏んで引く強い弩 (蹶張) が、北の騎兵に対する切り札となった。

西方にも古代ギリシアの「腹当て弓」のような弩はあったが、広く使われたのは中世になってからである。東アジアでは二千年以上前に、すでに弩が大量に作られ、組織的に使われていた。
body.en:
A crossbow holds the drawn string on a trigger catch until the archer has taken aim. Since nobody has to hold the draw with the strength of his arms, weaker men could learn it quickly, and it shot farther and harder than a strong bow — hard enough to pierce armour.

In the Warring States the crossbow became the infantry's main weapon. "All the strong bows and crossbows under heaven come from Han," it was said, and the crossbows of Han reached six hundred paces — so the persuader [[p:蘇秦|Su Qin]] is supposed to have told its king. The bronze trigger parts were cast so precisely that they matched and could be swapped when broken.

At Maling [[p:孫臏|Sun Bin]] hid ten thousand crossbowmen on both sides of the road and broke [[p:龐涓|Pang Juan]]'s army with a single volley. Crossbows are at their best shot together in ranks; men learned to take turns, the rear rank spanning while the front rank shot.

Among the terracotta warriors of the First Emperor's tomb kneel crossbowmen ready to shoot. Under the Han, powerful crossbows spanned with the feet became the trump card against the horsemen of the north.

The West had crossbows too — the "belly bow" of ancient Greece — but they spread widely only in the Middle Ages. In East Asia they were made in great numbers and used in organised ranks more than two thousand years ago.

body.ja:
戦国の初め、魏の文侯は[[p:呉起]]に命じて精兵「武卒」を選ばせた。[[p:荀子]]によれば、その試験は、三重の鎧を着て、十二石の弩を引き、矢五十本を背負い、戈をかつぎ、兜をかぶり剣を帯び、三日分の食糧を担いで、半日で百里を走ること。合格すれば家の税と労役を免じられ、田と家を与えられた。

呉起は兵と同じものを食べ、同じ所に寝て、馬にも乗らず、自分の食糧は自分で担いだ。兵の腫れ物の膿を口で吸い出してやったとき、その兵の母は声を上げて泣いた。「あの子の父も将軍に膿を吸っていただき、ご恩に報いようと退かずに戦って死にました。あの子もきっと同じことになるでしょう」。

武卒を率いた呉起は秦から河西の地を奪い、諸侯と七十六度戦って六十四度勝ち、残りも引き分けたという。魏は戦国の初めの最強国となった。

しかし荀子は武卒の弱点も指摘している。一度選ばれると、年を取って衰えても特権は取り上げられない。新しく選ぶにも費用がかかる。国が豊かでも兵の数を増やせない。呉起が魏を去り、馬陵で魏が敗れたのち、選ばれた精兵の時代は、秦の軍功爵による大動員の時代に取って代わられていった。
body.en:
At the start of the Warring States Marquis Wen of Wei had [[p:呉起|Wu Qi]] select an elite infantry, the "martial soldiers". [[p:荀子|Xunzi]] describes the test: in three layers of armour, spanning a twelve-stone crossbow, with fifty arrows on the back, a dagger-axe on the shoulder, helmet and sword, and three days' food, a man had to cover a hundred li by noon. Those who passed were freed from tax and labour and given fields and a house.

Wu Qi ate what his men ate, slept where they slept, would not ride, and carried his own food. When he sucked the pus from a soldier's abscess, the soldier's mother wailed: "The general did the same for his father, who would not turn back in battle to repay him, and died. Now my son will too."

Leading these soldiers Wu Qi took the land west of the Yellow River from Qin and fought the lords seventy-six times, winning sixty-four and drawing the rest, it is said. Wei became the first great power of the Warring States.

Xunzi also saw the weakness. A man once chosen kept his privileges even when he grew old and weak; choosing new men was costly; a rich state still could not field more of them. After Wu Qi left Wei and Wei was beaten at Maling, the age of picked soldiers gave way to the mass levies of Qin and its ranks for heads.

body.ja:
[[p:商鞅]]の変法で、秦は爵位を戦の手柄で与えることにした。敵の甲冑の兵の首を一つ取れば、爵一級と田一頃・宅地九畝、それに召し使う者一人。爵は二十の等級に分かれ、上がるほど田と税の免除が増え、罪を爵で償うこともできた。

反対に、王の一族でも軍功がなければ一族の籍から外された。家柄ではなく首の数が身分を決める——中原の諸侯から見れば野蛮だったが、秦の農民には出世の道が開かれた。秦の兵は戦場で兜を脱ぎ捨て、左手に敵の首を下げ、右脇に捕虜を抱えて駆けた、と遊説家の[[p:張儀]]は語っている。

五家を一組とする「伍」の仕組みもあった。一人が罪を犯せば組の皆が罰せられ、互いに見張り合う。農と戦のほかに出世の道はふさがれ、国全体が兵と兵糧を生み出す仕組みとなった。

この仕組みが長平の戦いのような大動員を可能にした。長平では、秦王が自ら河内に出向いて民に爵を一級ずつ与え、十五歳以上の男子をすべて送り込んだと伝わる。秦の統一は、この冷徹な仕組みの上に築かれた。
body.en:
Under [[p:商鞅|Shang Yang]]'s reforms Qin gave rank for deeds in war. One head of an armoured enemy soldier earned one degree of rank, a hundred mu of land, nine mu for a house and a servant. There were twenty degrees; the higher a man rose, the more land and freedom from tax he had, and rank could buy off punishment.

The other way round, members of the royal clan with no merit in war were struck from its register. Heads, not birth, made a man's place — barbarous in the eyes of the Central Plain, but a road upward for Qin's farmers. The soldiers of Qin, said the persuader [[p:張儀|Zhang Yi]], threw off their helmets and ran at the enemy with a head in the left hand and a prisoner under the right arm.

Households were grouped in fives: if one broke the law, all were punished, so all watched each other. Every road to advancement but farming and war was closed, and the whole state became a machine for soldiers and grain.

That machine made levies like Changping possible: the king, it is said, went himself to Henei, gave every man a degree of rank and sent every male over fifteen to the front. The unification of China was built on it.

title.en: The swords of Wu and Yue

body.ja:
春秋の終わり、長江の下流の呉と越は、名剣の国として知られた。青銅に錫を合わせる割合を変えて、刃は硬く、芯は粘り強く鋳分ける技があったという。

伝説の刀工も多い。越の欧冶子は越王のために「湛盧」「純鈞」など五振りの剣を鍛えた。呉王[[p:闔閭]]に命じられた干将は、炉の鉄がどうしても溶けず、妻の莫耶が髪と爪を炉に投じてようやく溶けたという。こうして鍛えた雌雄二振りの剣が「干将」と「莫耶」である。

1965年、湖北省の楚の墓から一振りの剣が掘り出された。刃には鳥の形をした文字で「越王鳩浅 (勾践) 自ら作りて用いる剣」とある。二千四百年以上土の中にあったのに錆はほとんどなく、刃は紙を何枚も重ねて切れたという。越の剣がなぜ楚の墓に入ったのか——嫁入り道具だったのか、戦利品だったのか——は分かっていない。

剣にまつわる美しい話もある。呉の公子[[p:季札]]が北へ使いに行く途中、徐の君主が季札の剣を欲しそうに見ていた。使いの途中なので贈れなかった季札が帰りに立ち寄ると、徐君はもう亡くなっていた。季札は剣を外して墓の木に掛けて去った。「心の中で贈ると決めていたのだから、相手が死んだからといって約束を破れようか」。
body.en:
At the end of the Spring and Autumn the lower Yangzi states of Wu and Yue were famous for their swords. Their smiths cast blades in which the proportion of tin to copper differed — a hard edge, a tougher core.

Legendary smiths abound. Ou Yezi forged five swords for the king of Yue, among them Zhanlu and Chunjun. Gan Jiang, set to work by King [[p:闔閭|Helü]] of Wu, could not get his iron to melt until his wife Mo Ye threw her hair and nail clippings into the furnace; the pair of swords that came of it bear their names.

In 1965 a sword was dug from a Chu tomb in Hubei. Its blade carries, in bird-shaped script, "[[p:句践|Goujian]], King of Yue, made this sword for his own use". After more than 2,400 years underground it was barely tarnished, and could still cut through a stack of paper. How a Yue sword came to lie in a Chu grave — dowry or booty — no one knows.

There is a gentle story too. [[p:季札|Ji Zha]], a prince of Wu travelling north as envoy, saw that the lord of Xu admired his sword. An envoy cannot give away his sword mid-journey; when Ji Zha came back, the lord of Xu was dead. He hung the sword on a tree by the grave and went on. "I had promised it in my heart. Should his death make me break my word?"

title.en: The fish and salt of Qi

body.ja:
周の初め、太公望 (呂尚) が封じられた斉の地は、海辺の痩せた塩の土地で、人も少なかった。太公望は女たちの手仕事 (織物) を勧め、魚と塩の利を通わせた。すると人も物も四方から集まり、斉は大国となった、と『史記』は書く。

斉の桓公を覇者にした宰相[[p:管仲]]は、塩を国の財源にした。海水を煮て塩を作らせ、国がそれを買い上げて他国へ高く売る。塩は誰もが毎日なめる。税を重くしなくても、塩の値で国庫は満ちる——後の時代まで続く「塩の専売」の始まりと言われる。

都の臨淄は戦国時代、七万戸を数える大都市となった。遊説家の[[p:蘇秦]]は、道を行く車の車輪がぶつかり合い、人の肩がこすれ合い、袖を連ねれば幕となり、汗を払えば雨となる、と賑わいを語っている。人々は竽 (笛) を吹き、琴を弾き、闘鶏や犬の競走、蹴鞠に興じた。
body.en:
When the Grand Duke Lü Shang was given Qi at the start of the Zhou, it was poor, salty, sparsely peopled land by the sea. He encouraged the women's crafts and the trade in fish and salt, says the Records of the Grand Historian, and people and goods came from every side until Qi was a great state.

[[p:管仲|Guan Zhong]], the minister who made Duke Huan of Qi hegemon, made salt the treasury's mainstay: brine was boiled down, the state bought the salt and sold it dear abroad. Everyone eats salt every day; with no heavier taxes the treasury filled — the beginning, it is said, of the salt monopoly that later dynasties kept.

By the Warring States the capital Linzi had seventy thousand households. Its streets, said the persuader [[p:蘇秦|Su Qin]], were so crowded that chariot hubs knocked and shoulders rubbed; raised sleeves made a curtain and wiped sweat fell like rain. Its people played pipes and zithers and amused themselves with cockfights, dog races and football.

title.en: The silks of Qi and Lu

body.ja:
斉の「紈」は白く薄い練り絹、魯の「縞」は薄く細かい生絹。どちらも天下に名高く、「斉は冠・帯・衣・履で天下を覆う」と言われるほど、斉の衣服は諸国に行き渡った。

絹は戦にも使われた。『管子』には、斉の桓公が[[p:管仲]]の策で、わざと隣の魯と梁の厚絹 (綈) の服を着て国中に流行らせた話がある。魯と梁の民は畑を捨てて機を織った。頃合いを見て斉が買うのをやめると、二国は食糧が尽き、斉に従うしかなくなった。経済で国を降した話として語られる。

魯の縞の薄さは、のちの言い回しにも残った。「強い弩の矢も、飛び尽くしたところでは魯の縞さえ貫けない」(強弩の末、魯縞を穿つ能わず)。どれほど強い力も、勢いが尽きれば何もできない、という意味である。
body.en:
The wan of Qi was a fine white glossed silk, the gao of Lu a thin, close raw silk; both were famous, and Qi, it was said, "capped, belted, clothed and shod the whole world".

Silk could be a weapon. The Guanzi tells how Duke Huan of Qi, on [[p:管仲|Guan Zhong]]'s advice, made a fashion of wearing the heavy silk of his neighbours Lu and Liang. Their people left the fields to weave. When the moment came Qi stopped buying, and the two states, out of grain, had to bow to Qi — a conquest by trade.

The thinness of Lu silk entered a proverb: "An arrow from the strongest crossbow, at the end of its flight, cannot pierce the silk of Lu" — even the greatest force can do nothing once its momentum is spent.

body.ja:
南の大国楚の墓からは、赤と黒の漆を塗り重ねた器や道具が数多く出てくる。酒を飲む耳杯、化粧箱、太鼓の台、そして角を生やして舌を垂らした不思議な「鎮墓獣」。湿った土の中でも木を守る漆のおかげで、二千年以上たっても色は鮮やかなままである。

漆の木から採った樹液を薄く何十回も塗り重ね、乾かしては磨く。手間のかかる品で、漢の頃の記録では、一つの漆の杯は銅の杯の十倍の値がしたという。

思想家の[[p:荘子]]は、若い頃、宋の蒙という町で「漆園の吏」(漆畑の役人) を務めていた。楚の王が宰相に迎えようとしたとき、荘子は「死んで廟に祭られる亀より、生きて泥の中で尾を引きずっていたい」と言って断ったという。
body.en:
The tombs of the great southern state of Chu are full of objects coated in layer upon layer of red and black lacquer: ear-handled wine cups, cosmetic boxes, drum stands, and the strange antlered "tomb guardians" with lolling tongues. Lacquer protects wood even in wet earth, and their colours are bright after more than two thousand years.

Sap from the lacquer tree is laid on thinly dozens of times, dried and polished each time. It was costly work; in Han times a lacquered cup was worth ten bronze ones, the records say.

The philosopher [[p:荘子|Zhuangzi]] was, as a young man, an officer of the lacquer gardens at Meng in Song. When the King of Chu offered to make him chief minister he declined: better to be a live turtle dragging its tail in the mud than a dead one honoured in a temple.

body.ja:
中国の鉄は、西方と違ってまず「鋳鉄」として広まった。高温の炉で鉄を溶かし、型に流して作る。青銅を鋳る技の長い伝統があったからだと考えられている。

前513年、晋の趙鞅らは鉄で鼎を鋳て、そこに刑法を刻んだ (刑鼎)。鉄の確かな記録の中でも早いものである。[[p:孔子]]は「民が鼎を見て法を知れば、貴人を尊ばなくなる」と嘆いたという。

楚の宛は鉄の名産地で、「宛の鉅鉄の矛は蜂やさそりのように鋭い」と[[p:荀子]]は書いている。戦国時代には鉄の鋤や鍬が農民に行き渡り、荒れ地が耕され、人が増えた。鉄の斧で森が開かれ、深く掘れる鍬で水路が引かれた。

鉄は大金持ちも生んだ。趙の邯鄲で鉄を商った郭縦は王侯と並ぶ富を持ち、同じく趙の鉄商人卓氏は、秦に国を滅ぼされて蜀へ移されると、臨邛の鉄山で再び財を成し、千人の召し使いを抱えたと『史記』は伝える。
body.en:
Iron in China spread first as cast iron, unlike in the West: melted in hot furnaces and poured into moulds — thanks, it is thought, to the long tradition of casting bronze.

In 513 BC Zhao Yang of Jin and others cast an iron cauldron and inscribed the laws on it, one of the earliest sure records of iron. [[p:孔子|Confucius]] lamented that once the people could read the law on a cauldron, they would no longer honour the nobles.

Wan in Chu was famous for iron: "the iron spears of Wan are as sharp as wasps and scorpions," [[p:荀子|Xunzi]] wrote. By the Warring States iron ploughshares and hoes were in every farmer's hands; wasteland was broken, forests cleared with iron axes, canals dug with deep hoes, and people multiplied.

Iron made fortunes too. Guo Zong, an iron dealer of Handan, was as rich as a king; the Zhuo family, iron merchants of Zhao deported to Shu when Qin destroyed their state, made a second fortune from the iron hills of Linqiong and kept a thousand servants, says the Records of the Grand Historian.

body.ja:
斉の桓公は、かつて自分に矢を射かけた[[p:管仲]]を、親友の[[p:鮑叔牙]]に勧められて宰相に迎えた。管仲は斉を、春秋で最初の覇者の国に作り変えた。

管仲はまず民を四つに分けて住まわせた。士 (武士)・農・工・商。同じ仕事の者が集まって住めば、子は親の技を見て自然に覚え、余計な望みを持たない、と考えたのである。さらに村の組織をそのまま軍の組織とし (内政に軍令を寄せる)、五家が一組の伍は戦では五人の伍となった。幼い頃から共に暮らした者同士は、夜の戦でも声で互いを知り、死を共にできる。

国の財は海から得た。海水を煮て塩を作り、鉄を管理し、物の値の上下を見て国が買い入れ売り払う。管仲の言葉として「倉が満ちて礼節を知り、衣食が足りて栄誉と恥を知る」が伝わる。

桓公はこの力で諸侯を集め、周の王を尊び、北の山戎や南の楚を討った。[[p:孔子]]はのちに「管仲がいなければ、私たちは今ごろ髪を振り乱し、着物を左前に着ていただろう (夷狄の風になっていただろう)」と言った。
body.en:
Duke Huan of Qi made [[p:管仲|Guan Zhong]] his chief minister — the man who had once shot an arrow at him — on the word of Guan Zhong's friend [[p:鮑叔牙|Bao Shuya]]. Guan Zhong made Qi the first hegemon of the Spring and Autumn.

He began by settling the people in four orders, each in its own quarter: officers, farmers, craftsmen and merchants. Living among their own trade, children learned it from their parents and wanted nothing else. He made the village the army, too: five households were five men in a file, and men who had grown up together knew each other's voices in a night battle and would die for one another.

Wealth came from the sea: brine boiled into salt, iron under the state's hand, and the state buying cheap and selling dear as prices rose and fell. A saying is put in his mouth: "When the granaries are full, people know propriety; when food and clothing suffice, they know honour and shame."

With this strength Duke Huan gathered the lords, honoured the king of Zhou and struck the Mountain Rong in the north and Chu in the south. "But for Guan Zhong," [[p:孔子|Confucius]] said, "we should all be wearing our hair loose and folding our robes to the left like barbarians."

body.ja:
周の昔の田は「井田」であった、と後の書物は言う。九つに区切った田のうち、まわりの八区画を八家がそれぞれ耕し、真ん中の一区画を皆で耕して、その収穫を領主に納める。

前594年、魯は初めて、田の広さに応じて一律に税を取った (初税畝)。共同で耕す田の収穫ではなく、それぞれの田から税を取る——言いかえれば、民が自分で切り開いた田も、その者の田として認めたことになる。『左伝』は「礼にかなっていない」と書いたが、流れは止まらなかった。

鄭の[[p:子産]]は前538年に「丘賦」(土地に応じた軍の負担) を定め、秦も前408年に「初めて禾 (穀物) を租とした」。土地に税をかける仕組みは、戦国の国々が民を直接治め、兵と食糧を集める土台となっていく。
body.en:
In the old days of Zhou, later books say, the fields were "well fields": a square of nine plots, eight farmed by eight families for themselves and the middle one farmed by all for the lord.

In 594 BC Lu for the first time taxed every field by its area. Not the harvest of the common plot but a share of each field — in effect, the land a family had broken for itself became its own. The Zuo Commentary called it "not according to the rites", but the tide did not turn back.

[[p:子産|Zichan]] of Zheng set a military levy by land in 538 BC, and Qin "first took grain as tax" in 408 BC. Taxing the land became the footing on which the Warring States ruled their people directly and raised soldiers and food.

title.ja: 法を民に示す (刑書と刑鼎)

body.ja:
それまで刑罰の決まりは、貴族たちが胸に秘めて、その時々に裁くものであった。前536年、鄭の宰相[[p:子産]]は、刑法を青銅の鼎に鋳込んで人々に示した (刑書)。

晋の賢人[[p:叔向]]は子産に手紙を送って責めた。「民が法を知れば、上を恐れず、条文を盾に争うようになる。国は滅びるだろう」。子産は短く答えた。「私には子孫のことまで考える才はない。ただ世を救うためにするのだ」。

前513年には晋も、趙鞅らが鉄の鼎に刑法を鋳込んだ。[[p:孔子]]は「民が鼎を見て法を知れば、貴人を尊ぶだろうか」と嘆いたという。

鄭ではさらに、[[p:鄧析]]という人が竹簡に法を書き写した「竹刑」を作り、人々の訴えを手伝った。鄧析は前501年に処刑されたが、その竹刑は使われ続けた。法を誰もが読めるものにする流れは、戦国の法家へとつながっていく。
body.en:
Until then the rules of punishment were kept in the nobles' heads and applied as they saw fit. In 536 BC [[p:子産|Zichan]], chief minister of Zheng, cast the laws on bronze cauldrons for all to see.

[[p:叔向|Shuxiang]], the wise man of Jin, wrote to rebuke him: "When the people know the law they will not fear their betters; they will quarrel over its words, and the state will perish." Zichan replied briefly: "I lack the talent to think of my descendants. I do it to save the present age."

In 513 BC Jin too, under Zhao Yang, cast its laws on an iron cauldron. [[p:孔子|Confucius]] lamented: once the people read the law on the cauldron, would they still honour the noble?

In Zheng a man named [[p:鄧析|Deng Xi]] copied the laws onto bamboo — the "bamboo code" — and helped people with their suits. He was put to death in 501 BC, but his code stayed in use. Making the law something anyone could read led on to the Legalists of the Warring States.

effect.ja: ゲームの中では、取り入れた国に一度だけ: 安定 +4%
effect.en: In the game, once for a realm that takes it up: stability +4%

body.ja:
戦国の初め、魏の文侯は[[p:李悝]]を用いて国を立て直した。李悝は「土地の力を尽くす教え」を説いた。同じ広さの田でも、よく耕せば収穫は大きく増える。勤めれば増え、怠ければ減る——それが国全体では大きな差になる。

李悝はまた「平糴法」を定めた。豊作の年には国が穀物を買い上げて値崩れを防ぎ、不作の年には蓄えを売り出して値上がりを抑える。農民も町の民も守られ、魏は豊かになった。

李悝がまとめた『法経』六篇 (盗・賊・囚・捕・雑・具) は、中国の法典の始まりとされる。[[p:商鞅]]はこれを秦に持って行き、秦の法の土台とした。「食は労ある者に、禄は功ある者に」——家柄ではなく働きで報いるという考えも、李悝のものとして伝わる。
body.en:
At the start of the Warring States Marquis Wen of Wei rebuilt his state with [[p:李悝|Li Kui]]. Li Kui taught "making the most of the land": the same field gives far more if worked well, and the difference, across a whole country, is enormous.

He also set up the "even purchase" law: in good years the state bought grain so the price would not collapse, in bad years it sold from its stores to keep the price down. Farmers and townsfolk were both protected, and Wei grew rich.

His Canon of Laws in six books — theft, violence, prisons, arrest, miscellany and general rules — is counted the first Chinese code. [[p:商鞅|Shang Yang]] took it to Qin, where it became the base of Qin law. "Food to those who labour, stipends to those of merit" — reward by deeds rather than birth — is also attributed to him.

effect.en: In the game, once for a realm that takes it up: treasury +30, technology +0.02

body.ja:
魏を追われた名将[[p:呉起]]は、南の楚の悼王に迎えられて令尹 (宰相) となった。呉起は、楚が大きいのに弱いのは、貴族が多すぎるからだと見た。

呉起は、三代を過ぎた貴族の封地と俸禄を取り上げ、貴族たちを人の少ない辺境の地に移し、役に立たない役人を減らした。浮いた財で兵を養い、楚は南の百越を従え、北では陳・蔡を併せ、三晋を退けた。

だが恨みは深かった。前381年、悼王が死ぬと、貴族たちは葬儀の場で呉起に矢を射かけた。呉起は王の亡骸に覆いかぶさって死んだ。王の遺体に矢を当てるのは大罪である。新しい王は、王の亡骸を射た者を罪に問い、七十余りの家が滅ぼされた。呉起は死んでなお、仇に報いたのである。
body.en:
Driven from Wei, the great general [[p:呉起|Wu Qi]] was welcomed by King Dao of Chu and made chief minister. Chu, he saw, was big but weak because it carried too many nobles.

He took back the fiefs and stipends of noble lines three generations old, moved the nobles to empty frontier lands and cut useless offices. The savings fed soldiers; Chu subdued the Hundred Yue in the south, swallowed Chen and Cai in the north and drove back the three Jin states.

The hatred ran deep. When King Dao died in 381 BC the nobles shot at Wu Qi during the funeral. He threw himself over the king's body and died there. To strike a king's corpse was a great crime: the new king punished all who had shot at it, and more than seventy families were wiped out. Even in death Wu Qi repaid his enemies.

body.ja:
衛の公子に生まれた[[p:商鞅]] (衛鞅) は、魏で用いられず、西の秦の孝公に仕えた。前356年と前350年の二度の変法で、商鞅は秦を戦国最強の国に作り変えた。

まず民を五家・十家の組に分け、一人の罪を組の皆の罪とした。戦で首を取った者には爵を与え ([[a:qin_rank|軍功爵]])、王族でも功がなければ一族の籍から外した。成人の男子が二人以上いる家には税を倍にして、家を分けさせた。都を咸陽に移し、小さな村々をまとめて四十一の県とし、県令を置いて王が直接治めた。田のあぜを改め、升や秤の大きさを国中でそろえた。そのとき作られた青銅の升 (商鞅方升) が今も残っている。

法を信じさせるため、商鞅は都の南門に三丈の木を立て、「北門に移した者に十金を与える」と告げた。誰も信じないので五十金に上げると、ある男が移し、本当に五十金をもらった。

前338年、孝公が死ぬと、恨みを買っていた商鞅は追われる身となった。逃げて宿を求めると、宿の主人は「商君の法で、旅の証のない客を泊めると罰せられます」と断った。商鞅は「法を作った者が、その法に苦しむとは」と嘆いたという。商鞅は捕らえられ、車裂きの刑に処された。だが彼の法は残り、秦の統一の土台となった。
body.en:
Born a prince of Wey, [[p:商鞅|Shang Yang]] found no place in Wei and went west to serve Duke Xiao of Qin. In two rounds of reform, in 356 and 350 BC, he turned Qin into the strongest of the Warring States.

He grouped households in fives and tens and made the crime of one the crime of all; gave rank for heads taken in battle ([[a:qin_rank|ranks for heads]]) and struck royal kinsmen without merit from the clan register; doubled the tax on households with two grown sons, so that families split up. He moved the capital to Xianyang, merged the villages into forty-one counties governed by the king's own magistrates, redrew the field boundaries and made measures and weights the same everywhere — a bronze measure of his still survives.

To make people trust the law he set up a thirty-foot pole at the south gate of the capital and offered ten gold to whoever moved it to the north gate. No one believed him; he raised it to fifty. A man moved it — and was paid.

When Duke Xiao died in 338 BC Shang Yang, hated by many, had to flee. At an inn the keeper turned him away: "By Lord Shang's law, whoever lodges a guest without papers is punished." "So the maker of the law is caught by it," Shang Yang sighed. He was taken and torn apart by chariots — but his laws remained, the foundation of Qin's unification.

body.ja:
前355年頃、小国の韓の昭侯は、もとは身分の低い役人であった[[p:申不害]]を宰相とした。申不害が説いたのは「術」——君主が臣下を操る技である。

君主は自分の好みや考えを見せてはならない。見せれば臣下はそれに合わせて取り入る。役目 (名) を与え、その働き (実) が役目に合っているかを見比べて賞罰を決める (名を循いて実を責む)。そうすれば臣下は君主を欺けない。

申不害が生きている間の十五年、韓はよく治まり、兵は強く、攻めてくる国はなかったと『史記』は書く。のちに韓の公子[[p:韓非]]は、[[p:商鞅]]の「法」、申不害の「術」、慎到の「勢」を合わせて法家の考えをまとめ、その書は秦の始皇帝を感嘆させた。
body.en:
Around 355 BC Marquis Zhao of the small state of Han made [[p:申不害|Shen Buhai]], once a minor official, his chief minister. Shen taught shu — "method", the art by which a ruler handles his ministers.

A ruler must never show his likes or his thoughts, or his ministers will flatter him to suit them. He gives each a title and checks whether the performance matches the title, rewarding and punishing accordingly. Then no minister can deceive him.

For the fifteen years of Shen's life, says the Records of the Grand Historian, Han was well governed, its army strong, and no one attacked it. Later [[p:韓非|Han Fei]], a prince of Han, joined [[p:商鞅|Shang Yang]]'s law, Shen Buhai's method and Shen Dao's power into one Legalist teaching — a book that moved the First Emperor of Qin to admiration.

title.ja: 度量衡・文字の統一と郡県
title.en: One measure, one script, one realm

body.ja:
前221年に天下を一つにした秦は、国ごとにばらばらだったものを一つにそろえた。長さ・容積・重さの単位 (度量衡)、文字、銭、そして車の車軸の幅 (車同軌)。轍の幅がそろえば、どの国の道でも同じ車が走れる。

文字は[[p:李斯]]らが整えた「小篆」に統一された。銭は円い形に四角い穴の「半両銭」となり、のちの東アジアの銭の形のもとになった。秦の分銅や升には、統一を告げる始皇帝の詔が刻まれ、それが今も各地から見つかっている。

封建の諸侯は置かず、天下を三十六の郡に分け、郡には守 (長官)・尉 (軍)・監 (監察) を中央から送った。博士の淳于越が昔のように王の子弟を封じるよう説くと、李斯は「古を引いて今を誹る」と退け、やがて焚書へとつながっていく。

秦は十五年で滅んだが、郡県の仕組みと統一された文字は、その後二千年の中国の形となった。
body.en:
Having united the realm in 221 BC, Qin made one of everything that had differed from state to state: units of length, volume and weight, the script, the coinage — and even the width of cart axles, so that the same cart could run in the ruts of any road.

The script was standardised as the "small seal" worked out by [[p:李斯|Li Si]] and others. Coins became round with a square hole — the banliang, ancestor of East Asian coinage. Qin weights and measures carry the First Emperor's edict of unification, and they turn up all over China to this day.

There were no fief-holding lords: the realm was divided into thirty-six commanderies, each with a governor, a military commandant and an inspector sent from the centre. When the scholar Chunyu Yue urged that the emperor's sons be given fiefs as of old, Li Si rejected "using the past to slander the present" — the road to the burning of the books.

Qin fell in fifteen years, but the commanderies and the common script shaped China for the next two thousand.

body.ja:
魯の[[p:孔子]] (前551〜前479年) は、周の初めの礼と、人を思いやる心「仁」によって世を治めることを説いた。五十歳を過ぎて魯の大司寇 (司法の長) となり、夾谷の会盟では斉の企てを退けたが、まもなく魯を去り、十四年にわたって諸国を巡った。

旅は苦難の連続だった。陳と蔡の間では囲まれて七日も食べられず、弟子の[[p:子路]]が「君子も困ることがあるのですか」と怒ると、孔子は「君子はもとより困る。小人は困れば乱れるのだ」と答えた。晩年、魯に戻った孔子は弟子を教え、伝えられる弟子は三千人、うち六経に通じた者は七十二人という。その言葉は弟子たちによって『論語』にまとめられた。

孔子の死後、[[p:孟子]]は人の性は善であると説き、力ではなく徳で治める「王道」を諸侯に勧めた。斉の宣王が「私に王道ができようか」と問うと、孟子は、生贄に引かれる牛の怯える目を見て羊に替えさせた王の話を持ち出し、「その心があれば王になれます」と答えた。一方、[[p:荀子]]は人の性は悪であり、学びと礼で正すべきだと説き、その門から法家の[[p:韓非]]と[[p:李斯]]が出た。

儒家は戦国の世では用いられることが少なく、秦では書を焼かれた。だが漢の武帝の時代に国の学問となり、その後二千年、東アジアの政治と暮らしの土台となった。
body.en:
[[p:孔子|Confucius]] of Lu (551–479 BC) taught that the world should be governed by the rites of the early Zhou and by ren — humaneness. Past fifty he became Lu's minister of justice and foiled a plot of Qi at the meeting of Jiagu, but soon left Lu and wandered from state to state for fourteen years.

The road was hard. Surrounded between Chen and Cai, he and his disciples went seven days without food; when [[p:子路|Zilu]] asked angrily whether a gentleman, too, could be in such straits, Confucius answered: "A gentleman can be in straits; it is the petty man who, in straits, loses all restraint." Back in Lu in old age he taught — three thousand disciples, tradition says, seventy-two of whom mastered the six classics — and his sayings were gathered by them into the Analects.

After him [[p:孟子|Mencius]] taught that human nature is good and urged the lords to rule by virtue, the "kingly way", not by force. When King Xuan of Qi asked whether he could be such a king, Mencius reminded him how he had spared an ox led to sacrifice because he could not bear its frightened eyes: "That heart is enough to make a true king." [[p:荀子|Xunzi]] held instead that human nature is bad and must be straightened by learning and ritual — and from his school came the Legalists [[p:韓非|Han Fei]] and [[p:李斯|Li Si]].

The Confucians were little used in the Warring States and had their books burned under Qin. Under Emperor Wu of Han their teaching became the learning of the state, and for two thousand years the foundation of East Asian government and life.

body.ja:
[[p:墨子]] (墨翟) は、儒家の礼が貴族の飾りにすぎないと批判し、すべての人を分け隔てなく愛すること (兼愛)、攻めの戦をしないこと (非攻) を説いた。墨家は質素を重んじ、自ら働き、「鉅子」と呼ばれる長に従う固い団体であった。

非攻を説くだけではなかった。楚が名工[[p:公輸盤]]の作った雲梯 (攻城用のはしご車) で宋を攻めようとしたとき、墨子は十日十夜歩いて楚の都に着き、王の前で公輸盤と机上の攻め合いをした。帯を城に見立て、木片を武器にして、公輸盤は九度攻め方を変え、墨子は九度それを防いだ。しかも墨子の弟子三百人が、すでに宋の城で守りについていた。楚は宋攻めをやめた。

墨家の掟は厳しかった。秦にいた鉅子の腹䵍の一人息子が人を殺したとき、秦の恵王は「老いた身に子は一人だから」と罪を許した。腹䵍は「墨者の法では人を殺した者は死ぬ」と言って、自ら息子を処刑したという。

戦国の終わりまで儒家と並ぶ大きな学派であった墨家は、秦の統一の後、急に姿を消した。その書には、光や梃子の理など、古代の科学の記述も残されている。
body.en:
[[p:墨子|Mozi]] (Mo Di) attacked the Confucian rites as mere ornaments of the noble, and taught universal love — caring for all alike — and the condemnation of offensive war. The Mohists lived plainly, worked with their hands and obeyed a leader called the juzi: a close-knit order.

They did more than preach. When Chu prepared to attack Song with the siege ladders of the master craftsman [[p:公輸盤|Gongshu Ban]], Mozi walked ten days and nights to the Chu capital and, before the king, fought out the siege with Gongshu Ban on a table — a belt for the walls, slips of wood for the engines. Nine times Gongshu Ban changed his attack, nine times Mozi held. And three hundred of Mozi's disciples were already on the walls of Song. Chu gave up the attack.

Their law was hard. When the only son of Fu Tun, the Mohist leader in Qin, killed a man, King Hui of Qin pardoned him out of pity for the old man. Fu Tun answered that by Mohist law a killer dies, and put his son to death himself, it is said.

As great a school as the Confucians until the end of the Warring States, the Mohists vanished soon after Qin's unification. Their book preserves early science too: notes on light, on levers and on balance.

body.ja:
斉の人[[p:孫武]]は、呉王[[p:闔閭]]に十三篇の兵法を献じて将となった (前512年頃)。宮中の女官を調練して見せた話は、柏挙の戦いの窓にある。呉はその後、楚の都郢を落とし、北の斉・晋を脅かした。

『孫子』の言葉は今も生きている。「彼を知り己を知れば、百戦殆うからず」。「兵は詭道なり」——戦いは欺き合いである。「百戦百勝は善の善なる者に非ず。戦わずして人の兵を屈するは善の善なる者なり」。戦わずに勝つことこそ最上だ、というのである。

孫武の子孫とされる[[p:孫臏]]も兵法を書いたと伝わったが、その書は長く失われ、「孫子」は孫武ではなく孫臏の書だという説まであった。1972年、山東の銀雀山の漢の墓から、『孫子兵法』と『孫臏兵法』の竹簡がそろって見つかり、二つの書がともに存在したことが確かめられた。
body.en:
[[p:孫武|Sun Wu]] of Qi presented thirteen chapters on war to King [[p:闔閭|Helü]] of Wu and became his general (around 512 BC) — the story of the palace women he drilled is in the window of the battle of Boju. Wu went on to take Ying, the capital of Chu, and to menace Qi and Jin in the north.

Its sayings are alive today. "Know the enemy and know yourself, and in a hundred battles you will never be in peril." "All warfare is deception." "To win a hundred victories in a hundred battles is not the acme of skill; to subdue the enemy without fighting is the acme of skill."

His descendant [[p:孫臏|Sun Bin]] was also said to have written on war, but that book was long lost, and some even argued that the "Sunzi" was Sun Bin's work. In 1972 a Han tomb at Yinqueshan in Shandong yielded bamboo slips of both the Sunzi and the Sun Bin — proof that the two books had both existed.

body.ja:
斉の都臨淄の稷門のそばに、威王・宣王の頃 (前4世紀) 、諸国の学者を集める学宮が開かれた。学者たちには大きな屋敷と上大夫の待遇が与えられ、官職に就かずに「治めずして議論する」ことが許された。

集まった学者は千人とも言われる。儒家の[[p:孟子]]、のちに三度にわたって学宮の長 (祭酒) を務めた[[p:荀子]]、陰陽五行と「天下の外に大きな九つの州がある」と説いた[[p:鄒衍]]、法と勢を説いた慎到、ことば巧みな淳于髠。互いに論じ合い、ここで百家の考えが磨かれた。

「百家争鳴」——さまざまな学派が自由に論じ合う——の言葉にふさわしい場所であった。斉が燕に都を落とされた後も学宮は再建され、秦が斉を滅ぼすまで続いた。
body.en:
Near the Ji gate of Linzi, the capital of Qi, Kings Wei and Xuan in the fourth century BC opened an academy for scholars from every state. They were given fine houses and the rank of senior grandees, and allowed "to debate without governing".

A thousand gathered there, it is said: [[p:孟子|Mencius]] the Confucian; [[p:荀子|Xunzi]], three times head of the academy; [[p:鄒衍|Zou Yan]], who taught yin, yang and the five phases and that beyond the known world lay nine great continents; Shen Dao on law and power; the witty [[p:淳于髡|Chunyu Kun]]. Here the Hundred Schools sharpened their thought against each other.

It was the very place for "a hundred schools contending". Rebuilt after Yan sacked Linzi, it lasted until Qin destroyed Qi.

body.ja:
戦国の世には、弁舌ひとつで諸侯を説いて回り、国と国を結ばせたり裂いたりする遊説家がいた。南北に六国を結んで秦に当たる「合従」の[[p:蘇秦]]と、六国を一つずつ秦と結ばせて切り崩す「連衡」の[[p:張儀]]が、その代表である。二人は同じ[[p:鬼谷子]]に学んだと伝わる。

蘇秦は初め秦に用いられず、ぼろをまとって家に帰ると、妻は機から降りず、兄嫁は飯を炊かず、父母は口もきかなかった。蘇秦は夜も書を読み、眠くなると錐で股を刺した。やがて六国の相を兼ねる身となって故郷を通ると、兄嫁は這って迎えた。「なぜ前は傲慢で、今は恭しいのか」と問うと、兄嫁は「あなたが偉くなり、お金持ちになったからです」と答えたという。

張儀は若い頃、楚の宰相の宝玉を盗んだと疑われ、むち打たれて帰った。妻が嘆くと、張儀は「わたしの舌はまだあるか」と聞き、「あります」と聞くと「それで十分だ」と言った。のちに秦の宰相となった張儀は、斉と手を切れば秦の地六百里を与えると楚の懐王をだまし、楚が斉と絶交すると「約束したのは六里だ」と言い放った。
body.en:
The Warring States had their roving persuaders, who went from court to court and with their tongues alone bound states together or broke them apart. The greatest were [[p:蘇秦|Su Qin]], who joined the six states north to south against Qin — the Vertical Alliance — and [[p:張儀|Zhang Yi]], who picked them off one by one into alliances with Qin — the Horizontal. Both, tradition says, studied under the Master of Ghost Valley.

Su Qin at first found no favour in Qin and came home in rags: his wife would not leave her loom, his sister-in-law would not cook for him, his parents would not speak to him. He read through the nights, jabbing his thigh with an awl to stay awake. When he later passed through his home town as chief minister of six states, his sister-in-law crawled to greet him. Asked why she had been haughty then and humble now, she said: "Because you are great and rich."

As a young man Zhang Yi was suspected of stealing a jade from the chief minister of Chu and flogged. When his wife wept he asked, "Is my tongue still there?" — "It is." — "That is enough." Later, as Qin's chief minister, he promised King Huai of Chu six hundred li of land if Chu broke with Qi; when Chu had broken with Qi, he said: "I promised six li."
